sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa
Core: Organon, Materia Medica and Pharmacy

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Until the bridge was built, the village on the island was reached by a ferry that crossed every half hour and stopped at ten at night. Islanders planned their days around it. A wedding guest left before the last boat; a patient who fell ill at midnight waited for dawn. In return, the island kept a quiet that the mainland had lost. No lorry could reach it, no stranger arrived by accident, and land was worth only what it could grow.

The bridge changed the arithmetic in a single season. The journey to the town fell from an hour to ten minutes, and it could be made at any time. Children enrolled in colleges that had been out of reach. A man could hold a job in the city and sleep in his own house. Few islanders would give these things back.

Yet the same road that carried them out brought the mainland in. Within a few years paddy fields near the bridge had been sold for housing, at prices that made farming them seem foolish. The ferry had been an inconvenience, but it had also been a filter, and nobody had thought of it that way until it was gone. What the island learnt is that a connection cannot be ordered in one direction only. The planners had measured the minutes saved. No one had been asked to measure what the delay had been protecting.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: A department reports that a certificate now takes, on average, seven days to issue. The figure is true and tells an applicant very little. An average of seven days is what one gets when nine applications are cleared in two days and the tenth takes fifty-two. For nine people the office is fast. For the tenth it has, in effect, stopped working, and the average hides her completely.

Offices like averages because a single number is easy to report and easy to improve. Clearing the simple cases faster brings the average down, even if the difficult ones wait longer than ever. An officer judged on the average therefore has every reason to attend first to the files that need him least.

A different question gives a more honest picture: how long did the slowest tenth of applicants wait? This figure cannot be improved by hurrying the easy cases. It moves only when someone opens the files at the bottom of the pile and finds out why they are there: a missing signature, a disputed record, a query nobody answered. These are usually the cases where the applicant has least ability to push, and where a delay does the most harm. Measuring the slowest cases is a way of making the office look where it would rather not.

questions.q: Before the bridge, the quiet of the island was due mainly to:
opts: the small number of people living there
a ban on vehicles imposed by the panchayat
questions.why: No lorry could reach it and no stranger arrived by accident; the ferry limited access.

questions.q: Which of the following is given as a benefit of the bridge?
opts: Residents could work in the city and still live at home
questions.why: A man could hold a job in the city and sleep in his own house.

questions.q: The ferry is called 'a filter' because it:
opts: limited who and what could reach the island
charged a fare for each crossing
questions.why: As well as an inconvenience, the ferry had kept lorries, strangers and land buyers away.

questions.q: 'A connection cannot be ordered in one direction only' means that:
opts: islanders should not travel to the town
access that lets islanders out also lets outside pressures in
questions.why: The same road that carried the islanders out brought the mainland in.

questions.q: What is the author's criticism of the planners?
opts: They built the bridge in the wrong place
They counted the time saved but not what the isolation had protected
They ignored the cost of construction
They closed the ferry too early
questions.why: They measured the minutes saved; no one measured what the delay had been protecting.

questions.q: The example of the ten applications shows that an average:
opts: is always lower than the true figure
cannot be calculated for small numbers
can conceal a very long delay suffered by a few
is unfair to the nine quick cases
questions.why: Nine cleared in two days and one in fifty-two still average seven days, hiding the tenth applicant.

questions.q: Why, according to the passage, do offices like averages?
opts: A single number is easy to report and easy to improve
questions.why: The second paragraph gives exactly this reason.

questions.q: An officer who is judged on the average is tempted to:
opts: deal first with the simple files
questions.why: Clearing simple cases faster brings the average down, so he attends first to the files that need him least.

questions.q: Measuring the wait of the slowest tenth is a better test because that figure:
opts: improves only when the difficult cases are dealt with
is always smaller than the average
does not depend on the staff
questions.why: It cannot be improved by hurrying the easy cases; it moves only when the bottom of the pile is opened.

questions.q: According to the passage, the slowest cases often involve applicants who:
opts: are least able to press for attention
questions.why: These are usually the cases where the applicant has least ability to push.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: He divided the sweets ______ the four children.
questions.why: 'Among' is used for more than two; 'between' for two.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: It is high time we ______ the old records.
questions.why: 'It is high time' is followed by the simple past.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The more you practise, ______ you become.
questions.why: The pattern is 'the + comparative ..., the + comparative'.

questions.q: Which part of the sentence contains an error? Being a rainy day (A) / we decided (B) / to postpone (C) / the survey (D).
questions.why: As written, 'being a rainy day' describes 'we'. It should read 'It being a rainy day'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: He would rather ______ than apologise.
questions.why: 'Would rather' is followed by the verb without 'to'.

questions.q: Who chairs the Eighth Central Pay Commission, whose terms of reference were approved in October 2025?
questions.why: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the Commission. Justice A. K. Mathur chaired the Seventh.

questions.q: Goa was the second State to be declared fully literate under the ULLAS programme. Which State was the first?
questions.why: Mizoram was declared fully literate on 20 May 2025, ten days before Goa.

questions.q: Who was named Player of the Tournament at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026?
questions.why: Sanju Samson scored 321 runs. Jasprit Bumrah was Player of the Match in the final.

questions.q: Which is the largest wildlife sanctuary in Goa?
questions.why: Bhagwan Mahavir, which includes Mollem National Park, covers about 240 square kilometres. Bondla is the smallest.

questions.q: The international airport at Mopa is named after:
questions.why: It is Manohar International Airport, named after the former Chief Minister and Defence Minister.

questions.q: Which town is the headquarters of Bardez taluka?
questions.why: Mapusa is the taluka headquarters and is known for its Friday market.

questions.q: Under the Goa, Daman and Diu Official Language Act, 1987, Konkani in which script is the official language?
questions.why: The Act makes Konkani in the Devanagari script the official language.

questions.q: Article 352 of the Constitution deals with:
questions.why: Article 356 covers President's Rule, Article 360 Financial Emergency and Article 368 amendment.

questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.why: It was launched on 8 August 1942 at Bombay.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in:
questions.why: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 and was nationalised in 1949.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
questions.why: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.q: If '+' means multiply, 'x' means subtract, '-' means divide and '/' means add, what is the value of 8 + 6 x 12 - 4 / 5?
questions.why: After substitution: 8 x 6 - 12 / 4 + 5 = 48 - 3 + 5 = 50.

questions.q: Konkani is to Goa as Malayalam is to:
questions.why: Konkani is the official language of Goa; Malayalam of Kerala.

questions.q: The words Record, Recount, Receipt, Recall and Recent are arranged as in a dictionary. Which word comes third?
questions.why: The order is Recall, Receipt, Recent, Record, Recount.

questions.q: A's mother is the only daughter of B's father. If B is a man, how is B related to A?
questions.why: B's father's only daughter is B's sister. She is A's mother, so B is A's maternal uncle.

questions.q: Town P is 12 km due north of town Q. Town R is 5 km due west of P. What is the shortest distance between Q and R?
questions.why: The two legs are at right angles: the square root of 144 + 25 = 169, which is 13 km.

questions.q: Anil scored more than Bala but less than Chetan. Dev scored more than Chetan. Esha scored the least of the five. Who scored the second highest?
questions.why: In descending order: Dev, Chetan, Anil, Bala, Esha.

questions.q: Statements: No file is a register. Some registers are old. Conclusions: I. Some old things are not files. II. No old thing is a file.
questions.why: The old registers are not files, so I follows. Other old things may be files, so II does not.

questions.q: A clock gains 5 minutes every hour. It was set right at 8 a.m. What time will it show when the correct time is 2 p.m. on the same day?
questions.why: In 6 hours it gains 30 minutes and shows 2:30 p.m., not among options A to D.

questions.q: Statement: A sign at a railway station reads 'Use the footbridge to cross the line.' Assumptions: I. Crossing the track on foot is unsafe. II. Passengers can read and will follow the sign.
questions.why: The sign is put up because crossing the track is dangerous, and in the expectation that people will read and heed it.

questions.q: 'Similia similibus curentur' is correctly translated as:
opts: Likes are always cured by likes
Let likes be cured by likes
questions.why: Hahnemann wrote 'curentur' (subjunctive: let them be cured), a rule for the physician to follow, not 'curantur' (are cured).

questions.q: According to §6, the unprejudiced observer perceives in each individual disease only:
opts: the changes in health of body and mind that can be perceived by the senses
the material cause of the disease
the name given to the disease in textbooks
questions.why: §6: the observer, free from speculation, notices only deviations from the former healthy state, felt by the patient, remarked by those around him and observed by the physician.

questions.q: In Kent's observations, a quick, short and strong aggravation followed by rapid improvement indicates:
opts: a correct remedy and good vitality: the best prognosis
an incurable case with tissue destruction
a wrong remedy that must be antidoted
questions.why: Kent's third observation: the aggravation is quick, short and strong and is followed by rapid improvement, so the remedy suited and the reaction is vigorous.

questions.q: Hahnemann held psora responsible for what share of all chronic diseases?
questions.why: In The Chronic Diseases Hahnemann attributes about seven-eighths of chronic diseases to psora, the rest to syphilis and sycosis.

questions.q: Over-growth, warts, infiltration of tissues and aggravation in damp weather are characteristic of:
questions.why: Sycosis is the miasm of excess and over-production: warts, condylomata, thickening and catarrhal discharges, worse in humid weather.

questions.q: According to §150, a trivial ailment of recent origin (an indisposition) should be handled by:
opts: a slight change in diet and regimen, usually without medicine
an antipsoric remedy in high potency
a nosode of the prevailing miasm
questions.why: §150: a few trivial symptoms observed only a short time are not a fully developed disease; altering the diet and regimen will usually dispel the indisposition.

questions.q: The sixth edition of the Organon was first published, in German, in:
questions.why: Hahnemann finished the manuscript in 1842, a year before his death; Richard Haehl published it in 1921.

questions.q: 'The Genius of Homoeopathy: Lectures and Essays on Homoeopathic Philosophy' was written by:
questions.why: Stuart Close (1860-1929) published The Genius of Homoeopathy in 1924.

questions.q: The first remedy improved the patient; the improvement has stopped and the same symptoms have returned unchanged. The second prescription should usually be:
opts: a repetition of the same remedy
a new remedy chosen from the latest symptoms only
questions.why: Kent: when the original symptoms return unchanged after a good effect, the remedy is still indicated and is repeated.

questions.q: Rheumatic pains that are worse before a thunderstorm are a keynote of:
questions.why: Rhododendron: dread of storms, with pains that come on before a thunderstorm and ease once it breaks.

questions.q: Injuries to the periosteum and tendons, and eyestrain from fine work, call for:
questions.why: Ruta: bruised periosteum, strained tendons and flexors, and aching eyes after close work.

questions.q: Jealousy, obscene talk, a desire to uncover and foolish laughter point to:
questions.why: Hyoscyamus: jealous, immodest and obscene, with silly laughter and twitching.

questions.q: Which remedy is inimical to Rhus toxicodendron?
questions.why: Apis and Rhus tox are inimical and should not follow each other. Bryonia is complementary to Rhus tox.

questions.q: Ill effects of loss of sleep and night watching, with vertigo and nausea from riding in a carriage, call for:
questions.why: Cocculus: exhaustion from nursing the sick through the night, and travel sickness with vertigo.

questions.q: Profound melancholy with thoughts of suicide, and bone pains that are worse at night, indicate:
questions.why: Aurum met.: deep depression with a longing to die, and syphilitic bone pains worse at night.

questions.q: Stitching pains, aggravation between 2 and 4 a.m. and swelling of the upper eyelids are characteristic of:
questions.why: Kali carb.: stitching pains, the 2 to 4 a.m. aggravation, and baggy swelling of the upper lids.

questions.q: Profuse, offensive sweat that brings no relief, aggravation at night, and a moist, flabby, indented tongue with intense thirst point to:
questions.why: Mercurius: worse at night and from the heat of the bed, sweats without relief, and has the moist tongue with thirst.

questions.q: Which of the following is an imponderable?
questions.why: Imponderabilia are drugs prepared from energy, such as X-ray, magnetism and electricity.

questions.q: Nosodes are prepared from:
questions.why: Nosodes come from diseased material, such as Psorinum, Medorrhinum and Tuberculinum. Healthy tissues give sarcodes.

questions.q: By Hahnemann's method, how long does the trituration of one centesimal potency take?
questions.why: Each potency takes one hour: three periods of 20 minutes, each of 6 minutes' grinding and 4 minutes' scraping, done twice.

questions.q: After which trituration did Hahnemann convert a potency into liquid form?
questions.why: After the third centesimal trituration the substance is soluble and is carried on as a liquid potency.

questions.q: How many succussions are given at each step of the LM (50 millesimal) potency?
questions.why: The 6th edition prescribes 100 strong succussions for each LM step. The 5th edition used 2 for centesimal potencies.

questions.q: The first volume of the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of India was published in:
questions.why: HPI Volume I appeared in 1971; further volumes followed.

questions.q: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, which also governs homoeopathic medicines, was passed in:
questions.why: The Act dates from 1940. The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules followed in 1945.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a vehicle in homoeopathic pharmacy?
questions.why: Vehicles are neutral carriers with no medicinal action. Sulphur is a medicinal substance.
